## Request composition

The main session’s [base instructions](../../src/pi_secretary/src/instructions.ts) cover identity, Scopes, task delegation, memory, feedback, and communication. Active UserInstructions append Master’s current preferences, defaulting to Simplified Chinese. Settings accepts up to 2000 Unicode characters; identical content keeps its version, and empty content disables the custom section. When Host claims an input batch, it saves MainPromptSnapshot, freezing instructions, tool declarations, and available Scopes; recovery reuses this snapshot.

[Main-session tools](../../src/pi_secretary/src/main-tools.ts) cover tasks (task_propose/query/control), memory (memory_search/read/propose_change), wakeups (schedule_wakeup/cancel_wakeup), and communication (MasterInteract). Tool descriptions define parameters and usage; system instructions describe working rules. The Scope list is limited to 64 entries and 8 KiB; shared notes are supplied as task material capped at 8 KiB.

The [execution prompt](../../src/pi_secretary/src/task-prompt.ts) uses a `secretary.agent-task.v1` package containing the round’s full goal, constraints, acceptance criteria, materials, Scope, and recovery receipts. Executors submit results through submit_result; documents, shared notes, and historical outputs are passed as task data. Summaries and Settings use the fixed-source compaction workflows in [summary](../../src/pi_secretary/src/summary.ts) and [settings-memory](../../src/pi_secretary/src/settings-memory.ts).

## Working memory and provenance

Consciousness stores the current working summary, commitments, and coverage references. MemoryExtractionJob stores full sources, event identities, successful segments, and retry times. CHECKPOINT stores recovery context; MODEL_REQUEST stores the request after budget projection. Provenance is linked through context, events, and memory versions.

[Routine maintenance](../../src/pi_secretary/src/memory-maintenance.ts) runs after 8 completed turns or after the first uncovered turn has waited 60 seconds, with a minimum interval of 120 seconds; task feedback can trigger it earlier. At 60% of available input capacity, context is compacted at a safe boundary; 80% is the forced threshold and 30% the target. New inputs remain queued while compaction works from fixed sources. Candidate commits verify memory version and provenance.

Sources are split into at most 64 segments; successful candidates are reused across restarts. A successful summary can commit immediately while commitment extraction advances independently. Failed segments retain their sources for retries; merging reads the latest commitment ledger. Settings follows the same provenance and projection rules; see [data flow](data-flow.md#memory-maintenance-and-settings) for application.

[MemoryCommitment](../../src/pi_secretary/src/memory.ts) stores a stable ID, original text, status, source batch, and resolution evidence. Result-reporting commitments are fulfilled by a matching TaskResult followed by genuine `notification.presented` evidence in the same session, with source batch, event order, and sourceEnd checked. General/composite commitments are explicitly resolved through `memory/commitments/{id}/resolve`. Legacy ExtractionRecovery remains readable; new extraction work uses MemoryExtractionJob.

## Removing original inputs from context and retrieving history

[selectInputProjection](../../src/pi_secretary/src/input-projection.ts) selects inputs consistently for routine compaction, Settings, and restart recovery. Removal requires a unique identity, full coverage by a successful summary or APPLIED Settings, exclusion from the current-turn and tool-protocol protection zones, and a caught-up PostgreSQL search watermark. The recent-original window defaults to at most 12 entries, also bounded by 15% of available budget and the remaining compaction target. If an entire entry is too large, selection continues with earlier originals that fit.

Removal receipts retain frozen coverage references and bounded-window IDs. Removed originals stay in journal/CAS; larger budgets or Settings rebuilds preserve existing removal decisions. If the index is unavailable, the last receipt is retained and new removals pause; uncovered inputs remain. Extraction failure does not revoke coverage from a successful summary.

| Tool | Read behavior |
| --- | --- |
| memory_search | [Literal substring search in PostgreSQL](../../src/pi_secretary/src/memory-search.ts): Master inputs, final replies, task summaries, notification bodies; filter by time `[from,to)`, kinds, scope_id, task_id; default 10, maximum 20; newest event first; returns snippets and event_id |
| memory_read source=log | [journal/CAS chunks](../../src/pi_secretary/src/main-tools.ts): by event_id; offset/length use Unicode code points; default 2000, maximum 4000; follow next_offset for full text and hash |
| memory_read source=consciousness | Current working memory |
| memory_read source=world | Query facts by subject (ID, name, or alias) and predicate; ambiguities return candidates; default 20, maximum 100; paginate with cursor |
| memory_propose_change | Submit ASSERT/CORRECT/RETRACT with source events; corrections/retractions include target_fact_id; the host assembles the contract and routes it through authorization and Settings |

Search status distinguishes not_configured, unmigrated, rebuilding, failed, and timed-out states; lagging results include partial and a watermark. Tool results are bounded by the turn’s remaining budget; shortened results include truncated and a continuation offset. World source_note is explanatory; evidence identity comes from source events.

## Model and maintenance retries

[durableStream](../../src/pi_secretary/src/transport.ts) sends at most three times per logical call, with delays of 2 and 10 seconds; a longer Retry-After takes precedence. Network failures, timeouts, 408/409/429/5xx, and overload errors are retried; authentication, parameter, capacity, and cancellation errors terminate separately. Attempt counts, request identity, and successful responses are persisted; recovery reuses saved successful responses.

[Maintenance backoff](../../src/pi_secretary/src/model-retry.ts) permits up to three retry rounds after the initial summary/extraction failure, after 5 minutes, 30 minutes, and 2 hours. Authentication, capacity, and source errors stop automatic retries. `session/compact` can requeue summaries; `memory/extraction/retry` requeues the extraction failures present at admission. `GET memory` reports progress; `memory/summary` and `memory/commitments` paginate content.

## Capacity and configuration

[budget](../../src/pi_secretary/src/budget.ts) estimates input using the UTF-8 byte upper bound of normalized text/JSON plus envelope overhead. Available input is `U = C − O − T − S` (window minus output, tool-growth reserve, and safety margin). Before sending, it checks `I ≤ U`; actual token usage is recorded with each call.

| Environment variable | Default or purpose |
| --- | --- |
| SECRETARY_MAIN_CONTEXT_WINDOW / SECRETARY_MAIN_INPUT_TOKENS / SECRETARY_MAIN_OUTPUT_TOKENS | Main-model capacity limits |
| SECRETARY_TASK_CONTEXT_WINDOW / SECRETARY_TASK_INPUT_TOKENS / SECRETARY_TASK_OUTPUT_TOKENS | Task-model capacity limits |
| SECRETARY_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS | 4096, normal output target |
| SECRETARY_COMPACTION_OUTPUT_TOKENS / SECRETARY_COMPACTION_RETRY_OUTPUT_TOKENS | 16384 / 32768, initial and subsequent summary targets |
| SECRETARY_TOOL_GROWTH_RESERVE | 4096 |
| SECRETARY_CONTEXT_SAFETY_TOKENS / SECRETARY_CONTEXT_SAFETY_RATIO | max(2048, 5% × C) |
| SECRETARY_COMPACTION_TARGET / SECRETARY_COMPACTION_THRESHOLD / SECRETARY_COMPACTION_FORCED_THRESHOLD | 0.30 / 0.60 / 0.80 |
| SECRETARY_RECENT_INPUT_MAX_COUNT / SECRETARY_RECENT_INPUT_BUDGET_RATIO | 12 / 0.15, ranges 0–100 / 0–0.25 |
| SECRETARY_MEMORY_UPDATE_TURNS / SECRETARY_MEMORY_UPDATE_SECONDS / SECRETARY_MEMORY_MIN_INTERVAL_SECONDS | 8 / 60 / 120 |

These parameters form part of the [Settings runtime configuration fingerprint](../../src/pi_secretary/src/settings.ts); existing contexts switch through compaction and rebuilding. Both main and task requests check capacity; exceeding it saves context and enters CAPACITY_BLOCKED.

## Wakeup inputs

[schedule_wakeup](../../src/pi_secretary/src/wakeups.ts) accepts a future time with an explicit timezone and up to 4 KiB of instructions, with at most 100 PENDING timers. At the deadline it saves an Input with producer=TIMER, containing scheduled/actual times, late_by_ms, and instructions. TIMER preserves identity through queues, replay, and Settings rebuilds; summaries and extraction distinguish Master from TIMER by actual input identity. Tool recovery uses stable receipts; the main session decides whether to notify Master based on the current situation.

## Current limitations

- New removals of original inputs pause without PostgreSQL or while search lags; long conversations may reach CAPACITY_BLOCKED.
- Capacity checks currently support openai-completions and openai-responses; actual payloads are checked again before sending.
- Scheduled wakeups are one-shot timers; FIRED/CANCELLED history is not yet cleaned up.
